newsitem.title: USA: Clinton bank bill eases some rev bond underwriting.
newsitem.headline: Clinton bank bill eases some rev bond underwriting.

text.p: The Clinton administration's new bank reform proposal would set less stringent standards for small banks when underwriting revenue bonds than larger, more sophisticated institutions, a senior U.S. Treasury Department official said on Wednesday.
"We recognize that revenue bond underwriting might be done by a great many smaller banks in local communities," the official, who asked not to be identified, said at a news briefing.

"We want to try to accommodate that without making that the occasion for subjecting a lot of banks to Securities and Exchange Commission regulation that (they) would not otherwise be subject (to)," the official said.
"But if the bank is engaged in more extensive types of securities activities it may cross the line where it becomes subject to SEC regulation," the official said.
The Treasury Department's proposal would not require banks to set up a separate securities affiliate to underwrite municipal revenue bonds, as have earlier measures.
